newsitem.title: INDIA: India steel, cement firms seen hit in first half.
newsitem.headline: India steel, cement firms seen hit in first half.

text.p: Indian steel, cement and car companies may take earnings hits but most other sectors should maintain profit growth in the first half of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), consensus estimates of analysts said on Wednesday.
Profits are forecast to grow by an average of 10.4 percent in the six months to September 30, compared to 12.2 percent in the year-earlier period.
Reuters polled 18 brokerages and securities firms on 27 top firms in the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index. The three companies omitted by the poll report results on a calendar basis.
"Beyond doubt there's an overall slowdown," said Sandeep Dhingra, research head at SSKI Securities. "Despite this we see earnings growth of 8.2-8.3 percent on year-on-year basis."
Cement and steel companies are expected to be the worst hit by slowing demand and shrinking margins with larger companies taking a bigger hit, analysts said.
Profits at state-run Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL), the country's largest steel firm, are forecast to plummet 69.8 percent to 1.1 billion rupees from 3.6 billion in the first half of 1996/97.
"When the chips are down your efficiency and size matter," said Dhingra. "SAIL is sitting on an inventory of 2.2 million tonnes which has a cost attached."
Tata Iron and Steel Company Ltd, the largest private steel firm, will see profits shrink 1.6 percent to 2.48 billion rupees from 2.52 billion, according to the consensus estimate.
Profits of Associated Cement Companies Ltd (ACC), the country's biggest cement maker, are projected to tumble 64.7 percent to 194.1 million rupees from 550.5 million rupees.
"ACC is very sensitive to price changes because it is in a huge turnover low margin industry," one analyst said.
ACC shares fell 108.25 rupees to 1,564 on the BSE on the consensus forecast, traders said.

India's largest truck maker, Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company Ltd, and the biggest scooter manufacturer, Bajaj Auto Ltd, are forecast to show negative growth because of an overall economic slowdown, they said.
But strong rural demand fuelled by bumper agricultural production and higher world prices for aluminium and petrochemicals was helping some sectors, analysts said.
Utility vehicles maker Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd is projected to see its net profit jump 31.1 percent to 1.2 billion rupees in the first half, thanks to buoyant rural demand for its tractors.
"I would recommend a switch to M&M in automobiles," said an equity salesman at a Hong Kong-based securities firm. "It's the star of the future."
Analysts expect company operations to improve in the second half as the economy picks up on the back of lower interest rates.
Banks have cut their prime lending rates by about 200 basis points over the past twelve months to 13.5 percent.
"I see better prospects in the second half," said Bimal Parikh, chief dealer at brokerage P.R. Subramanyam & Sons. "Interest costs which had squeezed profits last year will be reversed."
The second half would also have a lower threshold comparison because companies' workings in the year-ago period were hit by higher costs and falling demand, analysts said.
"For fiscal 1997/98 we are projecting earnings growth of 20 percent," SSKI's Dhingra added.
